text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Jordan affirms complete support for Palestinian Authority. King Hussein and President Yasser Arafat meet for comprehensive evaluation of peace process and ways to move forward and overcome obstacles.
- Jordan to discuss mining for gold and copper in Wadi Araba with Canadian company today.
- Parliamentary financial and economic committee calls on government to improve standards for military and civilian workers.
- Agriculture Minister Mustafa Shneikat permits imports of Friesian milking cows as long as they have been tested for diseases.
- Parliamentary session expected to be extended to allow for preparation of new election law.
- Minister of Communications Jamal Sarayrah submits resignation.
- King Hussein affirms Jordan's commitment to Palestinian independent will and respect for their choice.
- Jordanian-Palestinian summit discusses mobilising peace process.
- Six thousand Jordanian millionaires have investments worth $15 billion.
- Labour Minister Abdul-Hafez al-Shakhanbeh says everything in place for distribution of Gulf war compensations.
- Customs duty on mobile telephones to be cancelled. Cost of local calls to be cut.
- Sarayrah cites Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti's style of dealing with colleagues as reason for offering resignation.
- Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang returns home after visit to Jordan.
